pr_title: vo_gpu: hwdec: load hwdec interops on-demand by default
pr_body:
Historically, we have treated hwdec interop loading as a completely
separate step from loading the hwdecs themselves. Some hwdecs need an
interop, and some don't, and users generally configure the exact
hwdec they want, so interops that aren't relevant for that hwdec
shouldn't be loaded to save time and avoid warning/error spam.

The basic approach here is to recognise that interops are tied to
hwdecs by imgfmt. The hwdec outputs some format, and an interop is
needed to get that format to the vo without read back.

So, when we try to load an hwdec, instead of just blindly loading all
interops as we do today, let's pass the imgfmt in and only load
interops that work for that format. If more than one interop is
available for the format, the existing logic (whatever it is) will
continue to be used to pick one.

We also have one callsite in filters where we seem to pre-emptively
load all the interops. It's probably possible to trace down a specific
format but for now I'm just letting it keep loading all of them; it's
no worse than before.

You may notice there is no documentation update - and that's because
the current docs say that when the interop mode is `auto`, the interop
is loaded on demand. So reality now reflects the docs. How nice.

Fixes #8765
Fixes #9691
pr_comments: Updated to ensure we check for already loaded hwdecs in all scenarios.
Thanks, I'll tweak that to make it more consistent.

Finished my testing with:

1. `vo_libmpv` (macOS), which is the only one calling `gl_video_load_hwdecs` with `load_all_by_default` set to true.
   `mpv --no-config --hwdec=videotoolbox FILE`
2. `d3d11va` with `d3d11vp` (just to test one of the VPP filter usages).
    `mpv -v --no-config --hwdec=d3d11va --vf=d3d11vpp --hwdec-codecs=mpeg2video random_broadcast.ts`

Both seem to work :)

> Thanks, I'll tweak that to make it more consistent.

For the record, I'm not sure if the inconsistency is a problem, since it just makes sure that what gets loaded by VO preinit (at least with the GPU and libmpv VOs) is then all that gets loaded in case an interop is specified or set to no.

Just thought it was worth bringing up as a difference, though.

issue_context.title: Option to disable cuda-nvdec when no CUDA device present
issue_context.body:
### Important Information

Provide following Information:
- mpv version: 0.33.1
- Linux Distribution and Version: Archlinux
- Source of the mpv binary: Archlinux repository
- Window Manager and version: sway 0.16 
- GPU driver and version: Intel Tiger Lake, Mesa 21.0

### Reproduction steps

1. Have a device with CUDA installed, but no Nvidia GPU present and a device that supports hwdec=vaapi
2. Launch mpv on any video with hwdec=vaapi.

### Expected behavior
Video plays instantly using the device that supports vaapi. 

### Actual behavior
Video starts playing using the vaapi device after a delay of 10 seconds. Log shows that it gets stuck trying to initialize cuda-nvdec.

### Log file

https://0x0.st/-mPB.txt
comments:
I tried similar setup in a VM without CUDA device and installed nvidia-cuda-toolkit, however the initialization failure mentioned above doesn't seem to take 10 seconds, it seems to fast enough in my case.

It is possible to build mpv from source with cuda disabled:
`./waf configure --disable-cuda-hwaccel`

With the above mentioned build configuration, `cu->cuInit` call doesn't appear in the logs when `--hwdec=vaapi` is set.

I have the same issue. To note though that I have an nvidia card installed but the driver blacklisted (I use it to passthrough to a VM and load the vfio-pci driver via kernel command line to it).
I'd prefer the hwdec option in the config file to be honored and the cuda/nvidia driver not attempted at all even if nvidia/cuda software is installed and/or an nvidia card is detected (even if no nvidia driver is loaded).
For testing purposes I've deleted all library files from the nvidia-utils package which works around this issue:
`# pacman -Ql nvidia-utils | awk '/\.so/ {print $2}' | while read -r f; do [ -f "$f" ] && rm "$f"; done`
Log file with libraries exposing the issue at `Loading hwdec driver 'cuda-nvdec'`:
https://pastebin.com/raw/yexg42wU
Log file after workaround avoiding the issue:
https://pastebin.com/raw/bAPzcbt0
Though showing 'Cannot load libcuda.so.1' on the terminal even with `--really-quiet` option which appears to be this issue https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/issues/9691

review_comments:
I am not sure if this is a real case we have to think about, but what if the function gets called, but with a different imgfmt (from specific to none or from one specific to another would be the two cases that pop to my mind) ?

If switching of the imgfmt may only happen in case the whole gl_video gets reset, then just having a single boolean is fine. If we could have more and more things getting loaded with various calls, then just boolean would not be sufficient and we'd either have to have a bitmask or an array of bools...

I respected this boolean because if it's set, we know we loaded all interops. But if it's not set, we have a separate check for each individual interop to only load it if it's not already been loaded. So we can move between interops safely and also work correctly after a load_all happens.
